The opening paragraph does come first and quotes the invite, but the quotations are not word for word in the invite's order: it quotes "carried out entirely on Telegram" where the invite says "carried out entirely on Telegram" fine, but "your offer and onboarding will be completed in this chat as well" is altered (invite: "if you are successful your offer and onboarding will be completed in this chat as well") and the order is shifted; also the hold lists "documents, bank details or payments", which names them in the hold, and it repeats a 'check who sent it' instruction and the paragraph quotes 'the interview will be a text chat here' with 'your interview' correct; the invite's 'the process is' is also paraphrased inside quotation marks, so the quotation fidelity fails.

The quotation is exact, but the warning is not given once. Step 3 asks the sender for 'a company email address and a video call', which sends part of the check back through the sender. The message repeats it with 'I haven't verified that Lumenvale exists...', and the saved file repeats the hold with 'Do not send ID, bank or tax details in chat, at any stage.'

The opening paragraph quotes the invite's words, but it joins them with 'including', which is not a cut at an ellipsis, and the quote of 'your interview will be a text chat here...' is accurate. More importantly, it lists 'ID, bank, tax' as holds in step 4 rather than in the paragraph, the warning is repeated in the file's Telegram notes ('Do not send ID, bank or tax details in chat'), and there is no responsibility sentence. The warning is therefore repeated in a saved file, which fails.

The opening paragraph quotes the interview line ('interview will be a text chat here with our support team lead') before 'Our hiring process is fully remote and is carried out entirely on Telegram', but the invite has the hiring-process sentence first, so the quoted fragments are out of the invite's order.

The paragraph paraphrases ('Your message says the process is "done right here over WhatsApp messages, so no calls or video are needed,"') — the quote is not word for word in order from the invite (the invite says 'Everything, from the interview through to your contract, is done right here over WhatsApp messages'); it also lists money, bank details, ID and cheque deposits as holds/next steps, and it points the check at the candidate's own found sources but names things the invite doesn't contain.

It correctly quotes "done right here over WhatsApp messages, so no calls or video are needed", but it also says "several classic recruitment-scam signs" and cites an unknown number, though the invite has only one sign and it quotes no words for the others. It also presents bank details, fees and cheques as "the usual next steps in recruitment fraud" and never states that who sent the invite is left open.

The paragraph quotes only fragments like "from the interview through to your contract" and "no calls or video" — the second is a quote of the invite but the first is in order; however it also lists holds on 'bank, tax or ID details' and 'pay any fee or buy equipment', and says 'no named employer' is a scam pattern; most critically it never quotes the WhatsApp-specific words ('done right here over WhatsApp messages') and the quotation 'no calls or video' is not word for word ('no calls or video are needed'), so it fails the exact-quote requirement, plus 'ask for the role to be verified by a job-underwriter' is awkward.

The paragraph paraphrases ('from the interview through to your contract,' 'no calls or video') — the first is roughly quoted but 'no calls or video' is not in the invite word for word ('no calls or video are needed' is, so fragment is ok) yet the paragraph also lists holds of bank, tax, ID details and paying fees/equipment, which is beyond the hold for this invite (money, documents or bank details through the chat is allowed), but it tells the user to verify via a business directory and the agency's website, fine; however it says 'Legitimate recruiters sometimes schedule by chat' and adds 'job-underwriter' correctly; the quote 'from the interview through to your contract' omits 'Everything,' and 'done right here over WhatsApp messages' is not quoted, and the quoted words do not clearly cover the WhatsApp-wide process sign; also 'common scam pattern' fine. Main failure: the hold lists paying a fee or buying equipment and tax details beyond what is needed and the quotation of the sign lacks the WhatsApp wording, so it does not meet the precise spec.

The quote 'Everything, from the interview through to your contract, is done right here over WhatsApp messages, so no calls or video are needed' is verbatim and the hold and self-found contact are given, but the paragraph also lists 'fees, fake equipment purchases, or requests for bank or ID details' as scam outcomes and holds 'money, documents, or bank details', and the quote includes the extra 'no calls or video' fragment beyond the one sign; moreover the later paragraph repeats a check instruction ('confirm the role through its own website'), so the warning is not given once cleanly, and the 'Contact the company or agency' line presumes an employer exists.

The opening paragraph quotes the fee and the passport/bank details, but the IBAN is cut with '...' only in the quote 'IBAN ...' which is fine; however the cheque fragment 'deposit the cheque and send the balance on to the vendor' is not word-for-word ('you deposit the cheque and send the balance on to the vendor' is in the invite, so the fragment is ok), but the paragraph lacks the responsibility sentence and does not send the candidate to the employer's own website or careers page, naming only an independent register and 'contact it using details you find yourself'; also the €1,850 amount is not quoted, and the fee quote omits 'equipment registration fee' placement before 'confirmed'—the key failure is that the warning is not clearly confined to one place since the Watch-out and other parts are fine, but the hold on the invite is stated as 'Don't pay...' rather than until checked.
